Issue: [bug] Dependency preflight installs redundant fallback parsers

## What happened

The runtime dependency preflight treats alternative parser chains as though every
parser were required:

- PDF extraction offers to install `pdfminer.six` when `pdftotext` is absent but
  `pypdf` is already importable.
- HTML extraction offers to install `beautifulsoup4` when the preferred
  `trafilatura` parser is already importable.
- When no parser in an alternative chain is present, the preflight installs every
  alternative even though extraction only needs one.

This disagrees with `DEPENDENCY_GROUPS`, where PDF and HTML declare
`any_of_modules=True`, and can trigger unnecessary prompts and network installs.

## What you expected

For an any-of parser chain, any available parser should satisfy the preflight. If
none is available and installation is enabled, the preflight should install only
the first (preferred) parser. Formats whose dependencies are cumulative, such as
EPUB's `ebooklib` plus `beautifulsoup4`, should keep installing every missing
package.

## Source document

- Format: PDF and HTML
- Pages / size: n/a — the bug occurs before document parsing
- Language: n/a
- Does `python3 scripts/extract.py --check` show the relevant extractor installed? yes; the runtime preflight does not honor the same any-of semantics

## Repro

The failure is deterministic by stubbing dependency availability:

1. Make `python_module_available("pypdf")` return true and
   `python_module_available("pdfminer")` return false, with `pdftotext` absent.
2. Run `prepare_dependencies(".pdf", "text", "yes")`.
3. Observe an attempted `pdfminer.six` installation despite an available PDF
   parser.

The equivalent HTML case occurs with `trafilatura` available and `bs4` absent.

## Environment

- OS: platform-independent; reproduced on Windows 11 and verified under WSL/Linux
- Python version: 3.12 reproduction; full Linux suite also passes on Python 3.14
- book-to-skill version / commit: `a6cad12`
